headline: Generalizable models of regulatory DNA and single-cell perturbation responses
label: Interpretable Genomic Deep Learning
summary: Preprints and publications now test whether sequence and perturbation models generalize and expose biologically interpretable internal structure.
synthesis: The common thread is a shift from raw predictive accuracy toward generalization and biologically grounded interpretability. In regulatory DNA modeling, a Muon optimizer is compared against Adam for pretraining Transformers on ENCODE cis-regulatory sequences, while GROVER is fine-tuned for replication timing across seven human cell lines with a multimodal sequence-epigenetic variant. xDecoder decodes genomic language model and S2F embeddings for few-shot personal expression prediction. In single-cell work, perturbation models are benchmarked on differential expression classification, where simple nearest-neighbor methods are evaluated, scLEMBAS constrains a recurrent network with protein-interaction priors, and Perturb-seq responses are decomposed and aligned with gene coessentiality. A review of sequence-to-function models highlights generalizability, interpretability, and failure modes. FusedFCR and CellCover pursue interpretable marker selection along developmental trajectories. The items are heterogeneous; the shared element is explicit testing of out-of-distribution behavior and biological structure.
